item_ground_truth.source_work: FIFA World Cup Final, Italy vs France, Olympiastadion Berlin, July 9, 2006
item_ground_truth.event: After a 1-1 draw, left-back Fabio Grosso — not even among Lippi's originally chosen five takers — converted Italy's fifth and decisive penalty to win the shootout 5-3 and the World Cup.
item_ground_truth.ground_truth_evidence: Governing-body site: FIFA.com, 'Grosso: I will always remember that I ended Italy's penalty-shootout curse' — https://www.fifa.com/en/articles/grosso-i-will-always-remember-that-i-ended-italys-penalty-shootout-curse (Grosso scored the decisive kick; original five were Pirlo, Materazzi, De Rossi, Del Piero, Totti). Scorecard: ESPN match page — https://www.espn.com/soccer/match/_/gameId/191983/france-italy (shootout order Pirlo, Materazzi, De Rossi, Del Piero, Grosso all scored; Trezeguet missed; 5-3). Cross-check: contemporaneous report — https://www.foxnews.com/story/italy-defeats-france-in-2006-world-cup-penalty-shootout
